newsitem.title: FRANCE: Emirates to increase ex-Paris cargo rates.
newsitem.headline: Emirates to increase ex-Paris cargo rates.

text.p: Dubai government-owned airline, Emirates, said it planned to increase its ex-Paris cargo rates by between five and ten percent on routes to Dubai and onward destinations, effective March 1.
Emirates last increased it ex-Paris rates in January 1996.
Emirates operates a three-times weekly Paris-Dubai and Nice-Rome-Dubai passenger services with Airbus 300 and 310 which can handle up to 12 tonnes of palletised cargo per flight,

"Economic development in Dubai, notably in the form of new hotel projects, is generating buoyant demand for European goods such as perishables and luxury items - for example, perfumes and garments," a Paris-based cargo official for the airline told Reuters.

Since November 1996, Emirates Paris cargo station has had a regular block booking on a KLM Boeing 747F flight between Amsterdam and Dubai - as a result of growing cargo capacity requirements, the official added.
Emirates ships freight between CDG and Schiphol by truck on a weekly basis.

"The outlook for 1997 looks bright with the strengthening dollar probably having a positive effect too. Given such favourable conditions and the fact that we do not plan to increase our ex-Paris cargo capacity, the climate is conducive to rate increases and we are optimistic that these will be reasonably well-received by the market."
